claims: four annual increases of 3% each ... 12% over the life of the agreement
whys: Four 3% increases compound to about 12.55%, not 12%. '12%' is the simple sum. Either say 'about 12.6% compounded' or present it as the sum of the four increases.
reviewerNotes: Confirmed. payRise says '12% over the life of the agreement', but four compounding 3% increases come to about 12.55%. 12% is the simple sum.

claims: the APS, where the median employer contribution is 15.4%: on a VPS 5 salary of about $128,000 the gap between the Superannuation Guarantee rate of 12% and 15.4% is worth about $4,350 a year
whys: 15.4% is the standard PSSap employer rate, not a 'median'. The 12% SG rate and the $4,350 gap are typed into prose rather than taken from the SG rate constant, so they will go stale silently.
constants: Superannuation Guarantee rate constant (lib constants) and APS superannuation data
reviewerNotes: Plausible. The superannuation text calls 15.4% the APS 'median' employer contribution, when it is the standard PSSap rate. The 12% SG rate and the $4,350 figure are typed into prose and will go stale; the arithmetic itself checks out (about 3.4% of $128,000).
